note:
The placement test behind the “I don't know” tile on the homepage (src/pages/einstufungstest.astro). The A1 set is also the quick check on /step-by-step.

Six items per level; the test draws two, so someone who takes it twice does not get the same sentences. Each item tests exactly one feature that is typical of its level and not yet expected at the level below: be, present simple, a/an, irregular plurals and wh-questions for A1; past simple, comparatives, going to, prepositions of time, any and present continuous for A2; present perfect with since, first and second conditional, the passive, relative who and used to for B1; third conditional, reported questions, past deduction, wish + past perfect, so…that and be used to + -ing for B2; inversion, cleft sentences, participle clauses, mixed conditionals, distancing (is said to have) and it's time + past for C1.

Only one option is right, and the wrong ones are not nonsense words but the mistakes learners really make at that point (I have a idea, more big, If I would have, I'm not used to drive). A test you can pass by ruling out the silly answer measures nothing. Options that a native speaker could also accept in some context (some in questions, that for who, backshift-free reported speech) are deliberately left out.

Answers and options use the straight apostrophe ' because the page compares the clicked text with the answer exactly.

A2.prompt: Look at those clouds! It's ___ rain.
Is there ___ milk in the fridge?

B1.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
If I ___ more money, I would buy a car.
That's the woman ___ lives next door.
When I was a child, I ___ play football every day.

B2.prompt: If we ___ earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train.
The streets are wet. It ___ rained in the night.
I wish I ___ to the party last night.
The film was ___ boring that I fell asleep.
I'm not used to ___ on the left.

C1.prompt: ___ I need is a long holiday.
___ the report, she sent it to her manager.
If I had taken that job, I ___ in Paris now.
The company is said ___ millions last year.
It's late. It's high time we ___ home.
